scope: remove per-request whole-schema work from the query hot path, one measured cause at a time
no change to concurrency semantics, no new database support, no real model calls

profiling.method: cProfile around a single in-process run_query at 1000 tables (scripted router, mock embedding, SQLite fixture), plus stage durations from the node event callback

top_costs_before.note: per-character Python loop inside estimate_tokens; two str method calls per character
one rendered identifier per column of every table in the snapshot, for a statement that referenced one table

changes.what: estimate_tokens counts ASCII and non-ASCII characters with two C-level passes (encode + translate) instead of a per-character loop
changes.equivalence: arithmetic unchanged, including Python's treatment of 0x1c-0x1f as ASCII whitespace and non-ASCII whitespace being charged as CJK

in_process_ab_1k.method: old and new implementation alternated inside one process on one fixture, 15 requests each, 2 rounds

changes.what: parse the statement first and build the sqlglot MappingSchema only for the tables it names, instead of every table in the snapshot
pitfalls_found: qualify normalises the AST before calling on_qualify, so the source dictionary must be keyed by the same normalisation; otherwise a legal MAIN.USERS statement is rejected as an unrepresented namespace
case-insensitive dialects (sqlite/duckdb) need a casefold fallback to resolve USERS against a snapshot key spelled Users
unchanged_behaviour: unknown table still fails with Table '<x>' not found in schema

changes.what: hand-written SchemaSnapshot.clone() replaces copy.deepcopy for the snapshot the extraction cache hands out
semantics: scalars shared, other leaf values still deep-copied so the clone cannot alias mutable state
created_at and the frozen duckdb_source_state are shared on purpose
values verified equal to copy.deepcopy via dataclasses.asdict

measurements.instrument: scripts/scale_load.py, pipeline scenario, scripted router with fixed SQL, mock embedding provider, single process
measurements.method: identical command and spec before and after, source switched with git stash on the same machine in one session
measurements.conclusion_on_lease: with per-request CPU cut by ~6x, throughput still does not grow with concurrency and P50 still scales roughly linearly, so the single-connection lease is not the primary throughput ceiling; the remaining work is GIL-bound CPU inside one process

verification.ruff: ruff check app/ tests/ -> All checks passed
verification.mypy: mypy app/ -> no issues in 191 source files

not_covered: synthetic schema and scripted router only: no real model, no real embedding, no end-to-end semantic or cost numbers
SQLite only; PostgreSQL/MySQL validation and introspection paths were not re-measured this round
100k tables untested; 10k remains outside the interactive range even after the improvement
multi-worker / multi-replica deployment is still undesigned; no concurrency semantics changed
context compaction still measures the whole snapshot repr against the token budget and therefore always exceeds the threshold at scale; left unchanged and recorded as an open measurement question
keyword retrieval is still an O(tables) scan (~0.9 s at 10k); no inverted index or precomputed subset

MVP checks.steps: all steps success, including ruff check ., mypy app/, the per-file mypy gates, the frontend contract and build, and pytest -m 'not real_database'

Real database acceptance.steps: all steps success, including pytest tests/real_db, artifact upload and Stop containers
